title: Learning What to Change: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Educational Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.30559v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Persistent tutoring agents do more than answer questions: they manage course files, practice records, and learner profiles that govern future lessons. In such stateful settings, knowing what to teach does not guarantee knowing what to change. We identify a pervasive failure mode, content-state decoupling, where agents deliver pedagogically sound responses while silently corrupting workspace state through unwarranted updates, missed prerequisites, or unintended side effects. Text-level judges overlook these state errors, whereas isolated tool-call checks break down because whether a write action is valid depends jointly on the learner request, prior state, and execution order. We propose State-Verified Reinforcement Learning, which supervises online policy optimization directly through verifiable workspace transitions. translated_title: 学习改变什么：面向教育智能体的状态验证强化学习
translated_abstract: 持久化辅导智能体的功能不止于回答问题：它们还需管理课程文件、练习记录和学习者档案，而这些内容决定了后续课程的教学。在这类有状态的环境中，知道“教什么”并不能保证知道“改什么”。我们发现了一种普遍存在的失败模式——内容-状态脱节：智能体虽然给出了教学上合理的回复，却通过不必要的更新、遗漏的前置条件或意外的副作用悄然破坏了工作区状态。文本层面的评判器会忽视这些状态错误，而孤立的工具调用检查也会失效，因为一次写入操作是否有效取决于学习者请求、先前状态与执行顺序的共同作用。我们提出了状态验证强化学习，通过可验证的工作区状态转移直接监督在线策略优化。在围绕每次工具调用进行状态快照的隔离沙箱中，由确定性验证器审计工具效果……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出状态验证强化学习，在隔离沙箱中通过确定性验证器审计可验证的工作区状态转移以直接监督策略优化，从而解决教育智能体“内容-状态脱节”导致回复看似合理却悄然破坏工作区状态的问题。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes State-Verified Reinforcement Learning, which supervises online policy optimization through deterministic verification of workspace state transitions in isolated sandboxes, addressing the content-state decoupling failure mode where educational agents deliver pedagogically sound responses while silently corrupting workspace state.
